gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Keychron puts the same 2,600 mAh battery in the magnetic K3 HE and the mechanical K3 Ultra 8K yet rates them at up to 55 h and up to 550 h. The low-profile wireless pick that has Rapid Trigger gives up about 90% of its runtime for that analog sensing. The mechanical boards that keep long runtimes (K3 Ultra 8K, K3 Max, G915 X) can't do Rapid Trigger, because their switches fire at one fixed point (1.3 mm on the G915 X).
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com (top result in both chats, uncited), geekgamingtricks.com (top result in both chats, uncited) and the cited NuPhy, RTINGS and Tom's Hardware pages. mkbguide already gives the K3 HE at about 55 h and the K3 Ultra at 'up to 550 hours'. It never says the two use the same 2,600 mAh battery, so it can't separate the cost of magnetic sensing from a bigger battery. It also doesn't explain why a mechanical switch can't do Rapid Trigger. geekgamingtricks covers the sensing difference ('tracks magnetic position' vs 'registers at a predetermined point') and Valve's August 2024 CS2 SOCD/Snap Tap rule, so those angles are already taken. RTINGS's low-profile page returned no article body when fetched. The cited NuPhy page returned HTTP 429 every time.
decides: This confirms the split ChatGPT made but adds a cost it never stated. For Rapid Trigger with adjustable actuation, buy a magnetic board: the NuPhy Air75 HE or Logitech G515 RAPID TKL (both wired only), or the Keychron K3 HE if you need wireless. The K3 HE's wireless comes at a cost: Keychron rates it at 55 h from 2,600 mAh, and Notebookcheck measured about 27 h at maximum backlight over 2.4 GHz. That works if you charge it every few days, not if you want to charge it about once a month. Chat 2's 'gaming' picks (G915 X TKL, K3 Max) can't do Rapid Trigger or adjustable actuation at all. They suit shoppers who value wireless runtime over FPS strafing.

findings.label: How a linear Hall sensor reads key position
findings.value: Output responds proportionally to magnetic flux density (continuous analog position, not on/off)
findings.source_title: DRV5055 | Ratiometric linear hall effect sensor with analog output | TI.com
findings.note: TI's own words: 'a linear Hall-effect sensor that responds proportionally to magnetic flux density.' This is the property Rapid Trigger and adjustable actuation depend on. I don't know which sensor part Keychron or NuPhy use; Keychron's K2 HE page says TMR sensors. This is a general mechanism, not a K3 HE part spec.
